summary: Provision 'research-sprint' project template with ephemeral Slack channels, linked Confluence space, and lifecycle automation
description:
Issue summary:
We need a reusable Jira project template named 'research-sprint' that automates provisioning of a Confluence space (sprint wiki), ephemeral Slack channels for the sprint pod, and a delegated admin group for pod leads. The template should include lifecycle automation that archives the Jira project, Confluence space, and Slack channels after a configurable retention window, plus an audit log export step.

Impact:
Research and experimentation pods currently create ad-hoc projects/spaces/channels which leads to inconsistent naming, stale resources, and audit gaps. This causes noise for platform admins and increases surface area for stale permissions. A template will reduce manual provisioning overhead and enforce standardized lifecycle and auditability.

Requested changes (what success looks like):
- New Jira project template "research-sprint" visible in project create flow with sensible default issue types and board.
- Automated Confluence space created with a sprint page template and page hierarchy. Space should be linked to the Jira project via project-space metadata.
- Slack provisioning: create channels with naming convention sprint-<pod>-<id> and private membership pre-populated from a delegated admin group. Channels should be marked ephemeral and have a lifecycle policy to archive + remove members after retention.
- Delegated admin group: create and map a group (group name: pod-leads-research) that can manage membership for the sprint's channels and Confluence space without full org admin privileges.
- Lifecycle automation: scheduled job or automation rule to transition Jira projects to Archived, archive Confluence spaces, and archive Slack channels after N days (configurable at template creation, default 90 days).
- Audit/export: when archiving, export audit artifacts (Jira issues summary export, Confluence export, Slack channel membership list) and push to a central S3 bucket or attach to the archived project. Provide a Confluence or S3 path in the project metadata.
- Security review checklist: ensure ephemeral channels are private, delegated-admin role scoped down to group management for these resources only, and audit exports respect PII handling policy.

Environment:
- Applies org-wide with default region: us-east (platform-managed). Staging implementation should happen in the internal-staging org before production rollout.

Acceptance criteria:
- A team can create a new project using "research-sprint" template and receive a Jira project, Confluence space, and Slack channels generated automatically.
- Pod lead (member of pod-leads-research) can manage channel membership and Confluence space permissions without needing infra team involvement.
- Lifecycle automation triggers at the configured interval and moves resources to archived state and deposits audit exports in the agreed location.
- Documentation (Confluence page) and a short how-to are published in the Platform Ops space.

Rollout plan:
1) Implement prototype in internal-staging and test with one research pod (approx 1 week).
2) Iterate based on feedback, run security review and compliance sign-off (2-3 business days).
3) Gradual rollout to internal teams, enable self-service in project create UI.

Security considerations:
- Delegated admin group must not grant org-level permissions.
- Audit exports must be stored in a restricted S3 prefix with access logs.
- Slack export must obfuscate any user PII; coordinate with Security for retention policy.

Related resources and references:
- Confluence runbook: https://confluence.internal.redwood/research-pod-runbook (staging copy will be created)
acceptance_notes: Template visible in project create dropdown
Lifecycle automation archived resources and placed export in S3
